record.original_question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold of dimension >= 3 admit a closed geodesic net whose underlying graph is a theta-graph, namely a graph with two vertices joined by three distinct edges?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.0.3. Is it true that each closed Riemannian manifold of dimension ≥ 3 has a θ-graph shaped closed geodesic net?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(M,g)$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) Riemannian manifold of dimension $n \geq 3$. A geodesic net on $M$ is a finite multigraph $G$ together with a continuous map $f : G \to M$ such that:
(i) the restriction of $f$ to the interior of each edge of $G$ is a (nonconstant) geodesic arc parametrized by arc length;
(ii) at each vertex $v$ of $G$, the sum of the unit tangent vectors at $v$ of the geodesic edges meeting $v$ (taken with the outgoing orientation) equals zero in $T_{f(v)} M$.
Such a geodesic net is called a closed geodesic net. The theta-graph $\theta$ is the multigraph with exactly two vertices joined by three distinct edges.

Question: Does every closed Riemannian manifold $(M,g)$ of dimension $n \geq 3$ admit a closed geodesic net whose underlying graph is the theta-graph $\theta$ (i.e., two vertices $p, q \in M$ together with three geodesic arcs from $p$ to $q$ such that the three unit tangent vectors at $p$ sum to zero, and the three unit tangent vectors at $q$ sum to zero)?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of existence of theta-graph shaped stationary geodesic nets on general closed Riemannian manifolds appears to remain open. While there are partial results (e.g., existence on manifolds with nontrivial second homology, where a geodesic net of length at most 3·diam(M) exists but may be a closed geodesic, two loops, or a theta-graph; and existence on convex 2-spheres close to round), no general existence theorem in dimension ≥ 3 is recorded. Recent work (2025) on generic density of stationary geodesic nets explicitly notes that such nets may degenerate to unions of closed geodesics, leaving the theta-graph existence question unresolved.

status_evidence.title: The Minimal Length of a Closed Geodesic Net on a Riemannian Manifold with a Nontrivial Second Homology Group
status_evidence.snippet: On any closed Riemannian manifold with nontrivial second homology there exists a geodesic net of length at most 3 diam(M) which is either a closed geodesic, two loops at a point, or three segments between the same endpoints.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: theta-type net exists as one of three possibilities under topological assumptions.

status_evidence.title: Generic density of stationary geodesic nets that are not closed geodesics
status_evidence.snippet: Embedded stationary geodesic nets are equidistributed in dimension n ≥ 3 for generic metrics, but results allow that the nets are unions of closed geodesics.
status_evidence.claim: General existence of nontrivial theta-graph nets remains unresolved in dimension ≥ 3.

status_evidence.title: Open Problems and Questions about Geodesics (Burns-Matveev)
status_evidence.snippet: Hasanov-Moroianu question: Does every metric on S^2 admit a stationary theta-graph?
status_evidence.claim: The theta-graph existence question is listed among open problems on geodesic nets.
